root_cause.text: A typo in `rose_kill_by_device()` used the total count `cnt` instead of the loop index `i` when accessing the local array of sockets, causing reads of uninitialized entries or out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch corrects `array[cnt]` to `array[i]` in the for-loop body. The commit message explicitly states: "The loop mistakenly indexes array[cnt] instead of array[i]. For cnt < ARRAY_SIZE(array), this reads an uninitialized entry; for cnt == ARRAY_SIZE(array), it is an out-of-bounds read."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a typo where the wrong array index was used in a loop, causing incorrect element access.
intent_record.what: Changed array index from 'cnt' to 'i' in the for loop body, so that each iteration accesses the correct element of the array.
intent_record.how: The loop now correctly iterates over the array of socket pointers using the loop variable 'i' instead of always using the fixed value 'cnt', which would have caused out-of-bounds or wrong element access.
